accepted.s: Benjamin Schultze translated the Telugu Bible in which year, before its printing at Halle?
accepted.x: Benjamin Schultze completed the translation of the Telugu Bible in 1727. It was printed at Halle in 1747.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the translation year from the later printing year.

accepted.s: The Telugu Bible translated by Benjamin Schultze was printed at which place?
accepted.x: Schultze’s Telugu Bible was printed at Halle in Germany. The translation was completed earlier, in 1727.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue to separate Schultze’s work from Carey’s Serampore publication.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. William Carey was associated with the Serampore Mission.
2. William Carey produced the complete Telugu Bible.
3. William Carey introduced Telugu typefaces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Carey’s work included the complete Telugu Bible and Telugu typefaces through the Serampore Mission.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements belong to the same scholar’s contribution.

accepted.s: Who prepared the systematic Telugu grammar published in 1816?
accepted.x: A.D. Campbell prepared the systematic Telugu grammar in 1816.
accepted.tq: Match the specific work with its author rather than with another colonial Telugu scholar.

accepted.s: The journal Satyaduta was published in 1835 by the:
accepted.x: Satyaduta, the first Telugu journal, was published in 1835 by the Bellary Christian Mission.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation associated with the journal and its place of publication.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Vartamana Tarangini was associated with Sayyad Rahamtulla. Satyaduta, Rajasekhara Charitram and Seesari Charitra were associated with different persons.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped literary associations.

accepted.s: Vartamana Tarangini, regarded as the second Telugu journal, was issued on:
accepted.x: Vartamana Tarangini was issued on 8 June 1842 and is identified as the second Telugu journal.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date to distinguish an early journal from later literary association meetings.

accepted.s: Who wrote the social drama Nandaka Rajyam?
accepted.x: Nandaka Rajyam was written by Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri.
accepted.tq: Test the author of a less frequently confused dramatic work.

accepted.s: Seesari Charitra, the Telugu rendering of Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar, was written by:
accepted.x: Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri wrote Seesari Charitra, a Telugu rendering of Julius Caesar, in 1875.
accepted.tq: Link the translated title with the author rather than with the original playwright.

accepted.s: Yayati Charitra, described as a kavya in pure Telugu, was composed by:
accepted.x: Yayati Charitra was composed by Ponnekanti Telaganaryudu in 1572.
accepted.tq: Use the work–author association to avoid substituting a famous classical poet.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly reflects the scholarly position regarding the first Telugu novel?
o: Kanyasulkam is generally accepted as the first Telugu novel.
Mahasweta is universally accepted as the first Telugu novel.
Veyi Padagalu is regarded as the first Telugu novel.
Rajasekhara Charitram is the standard answer, though Mahasweta has also been proposed.
accepted.x: The standard answer is Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s Rajasekhara Charitram, although some scholars have proposed Kokkonda Venkataratnam’s Mahasweta.
accepted.tq: Recognise the standard examination answer while noticing the competing claim.

accepted.s: The first foreign-language work translated into Telugu, as identified in this context, was from:
accepted.x: The earliest foreign-language translations into Telugu were from Arabic. Char Darvesh became Nagu Pakirula Charitra.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the source language from the later English and German contributions.

accepted.s: Char Darvesh was rendered into Telugu as Nagu Pakirula Charitra by:
accepted.x: Erramalli Mallikarjunudu translated Char Darvesh into Telugu as Nagu Pakirula Charitra.
accepted.tq: Match the original work, Telugu title and translator as a single chain.

accepted.s: Kokkonda Venkataratnam became the first Andhra scholar to receive the title Mahamahopadhyaya in:
accepted.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam received the distinction of Mahamahopadhyaya in 1907. He was also known as the Andhra Bhasha Johnson.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year to distinguish a scholarly honour from institutional founding dates.

accepted.s: C.P. Brown learnt Telugu from:
accepted.x: C.P. Brown learnt Telugu from Kodandarama Pantulu.
accepted.tq: Test the teacher–scholar relationship rather than the scholar’s published works.

accepted.s: Which of the following was associated with C.P. Brown’s work?
o: The first Survey of India in 1815
The complete Telugu Bible at Serampore
The administrative replacement of Telugu by English
accepted.x: C.P. Brown prepared Telugu-English and English-Telugu dictionaries in 1853. The other options describe contributions of different persons or state an incorrect change.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct contribution while rejecting work assigned to neighbouring scholars.

accepted.s: C.P. Brown’s Verses of Vemana was based on approximately how many collected poems?
accepted.x: C.P. Brown collected approximately 2,000 poems of Vemana and published them as Verses of Vemana in 1829.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the approximate collection size from nearby round-number distractors.

accepted.s: The phrase “Italian of the East” in relation to Telugu was first used by:
accepted.x: The phrase “Italian of the East” was first used by Nicolo de Conti, though it is associated in later discussions with Telugu scholarship.
accepted.tq: Separate the originator of a famous phrase from the scholar who popularised Telugu studies.

accepted.s: Who assisted Colin Mackenzie in collecting Kaifiyats?
accepted.x: The Kavali brothers—Borraiah, Venkataramaiah and Lakshmaiah—assisted Colin Mackenzie in collecting Kaifiyats.
accepted.tq: Use the group association to avoid confusing collectors with later editors and preservers.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Colin Mackenzie:
1. He reached the Amaravati Stupa in 1797.
2. He was the first Surveyor General in 1815.
3. He personally transferred the Amaravati Stupa marbles to London in 1797.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: 1797 marked Mackenzie’s first visit to the stupa; the marbles reached London decades later.
accepted.tq: Watch for a true date joined to an incorrect consequence.

accepted.s: Benjamin Schultze was associated with which mission?
accepted.x: Benjamin Schultze was a German Lutheran associated with the Danish-Halle Mission. He came to India in 1719 and returned in 1743.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct mission instead of confusing Schultze with Carey.

accepted.s: Which colonial scholar kept Telugu as an administrative language?
accepted.x: Thomas Munro kept Telugu as an administrative language.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative policy with the appropriate colonial official.

accepted.s: C.P. Brown edited and published the works of which group of classical poets?
accepted.x: C.P. Brown edited works of Nannaya, Tikkana, Pothana and other classical poets, helping rescue palm-leaf texts through missionary presses.
accepted.tq: Use the classical–modern distinction to identify the correct group of authors.
accepted.sec: Collection and publication of classical works → editor

accepted.s: The author of Asamardhuni Jeevayatra is:
accepted.x: Asamardhuni Jeevayatra was written by Tripuraneni Gopichand.
accepted.tq: Directly match a modern Telugu work with its author.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Musalamma Maranamu was written by Gurajada Apparao, not Tripuraneni Gopichand. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the single swapped author in a list of familiar work–author pairs.

accepted.s: What is the distinctive theme associated with Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam?
o: A bat carrying a Dalit’s prayer to God
A reformer’s criticism of child marriage
A king’s political struggle against colonial rule
accepted.x: Gabbilam, published in 1941, presents a bat carrying a Dalit’s prayer to God.
accepted.tq: Use the work’s distinctive thematic image to identify it without relying only on the author.

accepted.s: Kanyasulkam was first staged in:
accepted.x: Gurajada Apparao’s Kanyasulkam was first staged in 1893.
accepted.tq: Separate the staging year of a drama from publication years of other Telugu works.

accepted.s: Who is known as the Father of the Telugu Renaissance?
accepted.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is known as the Father of the Telugu Renaissance.
accepted.tq: Identify the title-holder rather than the person associated with spoken Telugu or literary institutions.

accepted.s: Which statement about Kandukuri Veeresalingam is correct?
o: He first rendered Kalidasa’s Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu.
He founded the Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1905.
He collected Mackenzie’s Kaifiyats as Surveyor General.
accepted.x: Veeresalingam was the first to render Kalidasa’s Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu. The other statements refer to different persons or works.
accepted.tq: Use the author’s distinctive literary achievement to reject swapped contributions.

accepted.s: Gidugu Ramamurthy is associated with which movement?
o: The Vyavaharika or spoken Telugu movement
accepted.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy is regarded as the father of the Vyavaharika, or spoken, Telugu movement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish spoken-language reform from literary, missionary and archival activities.

accepted.s: Jonnavittula Gurunatham was associated with the:
accepted.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham belonged to the Young Men’s Literary Association and helped promote the Andhra idea through the press.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the literary association from similarly named cultural institutions.

accepted.s: The Andhra Sahitya Parishat meetings at Rajahmundry in 1912 and 1913 were presided over by:
accepted.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam presided over the Andhra Sahitya Parishat meetings at Rajahmundry on 23 April 1912 and 22 April 1913.
accepted.tq: Match the presiding person with the specific association meetings.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Meeting of Andhra Sahitya Parishat at Rajahmundry under Kokkonda Venkataratnam
B. Founding of Andhra Sahitya Parishat in Madras
C. Second Rajahmundry meeting of Andhra Sahitya Parishat
D. Establishment of Vijnana Chandrika Mandali
accepted.x: The correct sequence is founding of Andhra Sahitya Parishat in 1911, Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1905, followed by the Rajahmundry meetings in 1912 and 1913; therefore, by the dates supplied, the chronological order is D, B, A, C.
accepted.tq: Check the years first; the supplied dates place the 1905 event before the 1911 founding.

accepted.s: The commentaries on Vasucharitra, Manucharitra, Kalapurnodayam and Vijayavilasam were associated with:
o: Members of the Young Men’s Association
accepted.x: Pattam Parabrahma Sastri, Ravipati Gurumurti Sastri and Juluri Appayya of Brown’s College wrote commentaries on these works.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution from the cluster of scholars and classical works.

accepted.s: Who preserved Mackenzie’s manuscripts and Kaifiyats after their collection?
accepted.x: The manuscripts and Kaifiyats collected by Mackenzie and the Kavali brothers were preserved by C.P. Brown.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original collectors from the later preserver.
accepted.sec: Collection and publication of classical works → editor

accepted.s: Which work was published by the Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1910?
accepted.x: The Vijnana Chandrika Mandali published Andhrula Charitramu in 1910.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its publication and year.
accepted.sec: Vijnana Chandrika Mandali and Andhra Bhasha Nilayam

accepted.s: Which of the following persons was NOT associated with the establishment of the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam?
accepted.x: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Munagala Raja were associated with establishing the Nilayam. C.P. Brown was a colonial Telugu scholar and was not among these founders.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider among members of the same institutional group.
accepted.sec: Vijnana Chandrika Mandali and Andhra Bhasha Nilayam

accepted.s: Which pair of leaders is associated with the library movement?
o: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
accepted.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao were leaders of the library movement.
accepted.tq: Match a movement with its leading pair rather than with scholars of another field.
accepted.sec: Vijnana Chandrika Mandali and Andhra Bhasha Nilayam

accepted.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was blacklisted after the:
accepted.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was blacklisted after the Rajahmundry College incident of 1907.
accepted.tq: Link the person with the specific incident and year.
accepted.sec: Vijnana Chandrika Mandali and Andhra Bhasha Nilayam

accepted.s: The Andhra Sahitya Parishat was founded in Madras in 1911 and later based at:
accepted.x: The Andhra Sahitya Parishat was founded in Madras in 1911 and later based at Kakinada. It also held important sessions at Rajahmundry in 1912 and 1913.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founding place, later base and session venue.
accepted.sec: Andhra Parishat and Kakinada/Rajahmundry cultural bodies

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Rajahmundry’s cultural significance?
o: It was the headquarters of the Danish-Halle Mission.
It served as Veeresalingam’s reform base and has been a cultural capital since Eastern Chalukya times.
It was only a centre of missionary printing during the nineteenth century.
It became a cultural centre only after the founding of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat in Kakinada.
accepted.x: Rajahmundry was Veeresalingam’s reform base, associated with Vivekavardhini, and has been regarded as a cultural capital since the Eastern Chalukya period.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines both historical dimensions without an absolute or limiting claim.
accepted.sec: Andhra Parishat and Kakinada/Rajahmundry cultural bodies

accepted.s: Vivekavardhini, which began in 1874 and criticised Kokkonda’s Sanjeevani, was associated with:
accepted.x: Vivekavardhini was associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam. It began in 1874 and criticised Kokkonda’s Sanjeevani.
accepted.tq: Use the publication’s controversy to identify its author and reform context.
